Chapter 9 • Newton-Cartan Theory

9.3 Stratified Atlas

  • To read off the physical content of Newton’s axioms, we work in charts adapted to the foliation, whose time coordinate is absolute time. A chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) is stratified if \(\mathscr{X}^0 = \left. t \right|_\mathcal{U}\), so that the absolute spaces are the slices \(\mathscr{X}^0 = \text{const}\). Stratified charts exist around every point4 and form the stratified atlas \(\mathcal{A}_{\text{strat.}} \subseteq \mathcal{A}\), so we can always restrict to them. In what follows, Latin indices \(i, j, k, \dots\) run over \(\{0, 1, 2, 3\}\) and Greek indices \(\alpha, \beta, \delta, \dots\) over \(\{1, 2, 3\}\). Between two stratified charts, \begin{align*} \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^0}{\partial \mathscr{X}^0} = 1, \qquad \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^0}{\partial \mathscr{X}^\beta} = 0, \qquad \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^\alpha}{\partial \mathscr{X}^0} \text{ arbitrary}. \end{align*} Stratified charts agree on when an event happens, but their spatial coordinates may move, rotate, or deform in time. See more on pseudo-forces at Section 9.4.

  • In a stratified chart, \(\left. dt \right|_\mathcal{U} = dx^0\) has constant component functions \(\mathtt{t}_k = \delta^0_k\), hence \(\big( \nabla_{\partial x_i} dt \big)_k = - \Gamma^0_{ki}\) and \begin{align*} \nabla dt = 0 \longleftrightarrow \Gamma^0_{ki} = 0 \quad \forall \, k, i. \end{align*} Uniform flow thus removes all connection coefficient functions with an upper time index. Of the \(40\) coefficients of a torsion-free connection in four dimensions, the remaining \(30\) are \(\Gamma^\alpha_{\beta\delta} = \Gamma^\alpha_{\delta\beta}\) (\(18\)), \(\Gamma^\alpha_{0\beta} = \Gamma^\alpha_{\beta0}\) (\(9\)) and \(\Gamma^\alpha_{00}\) (\(3\)).

  • With \(\lambda \equiv t\), so that \(\dot{\gamma}^0_\mathcal{U} = (t \circ \gamma)' = 1\), and the component functions \(f^k_\gamma(t) \coloneqq (dx^k)_{\gamma(t)}\big( \mathcal{F}_\gamma(t) \big)\) of the force, Newton II reads \(\ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(t) + \Gamma^k_{ji}(t) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(t) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(t) = f^k_\gamma(t) / m\):

    1. Temporal part: \(f^0_\gamma(t) = 0\) (\(\mathcal{F}_\gamma\) is spatial) and \(\Gamma^0_{ji}(t) = 0\) give \(\ddot{\gamma}^0_\mathcal{U}(t) = 0\), consistent with \(\dot{\gamma}^0_\mathcal{U}(t) = 1\): it carries no information.

    2. Spatial part: splitting the sum over \(i, j\) into temporal and spatial values, and using \(\Gamma^\alpha_{0\beta} = \Gamma^\alpha_{\beta0}\) (torsion-free), \begin{align*} \underbrace{\ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U}(t) + \Gamma^\alpha_{\beta\delta}(t) \, \dot{\gamma}^\beta_\mathcal{U}(t) \, \dot{\gamma}^\delta_\mathcal{U}(t) + 2 \, \Gamma^\alpha_{0\beta}(t) \, \dot{\gamma}^\beta_\mathcal{U}(t) + \Gamma^\alpha_{00}(t)}_{a^\alpha_\gamma} = \frac{f^\alpha_\gamma(t)}{m}. \end{align*}

    Only the whole left-hand side is a component function of the vector field \(a_\gamma\) along \(\gamma\); the individual terms are not, since the connection coefficient functions are not the component functions of a tensor field. Moved to the right-hand side and multiplied by \(m\), each \(\Gamma\)-term looks like an additional force, called a pseudo-force, which a change of stratified chart can create or remove.

4

Given any chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) around \(p\), \((dt)_p \neq 0\) implies \(\partial_\kappa \left[ t \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \neq 0\) for some \(\kappa\). Replacing \(\mathscr{X}^\kappa\) by \(\left. t \right|_\mathcal{U}\) as zeroth coordinate gives a transition map with Jacobian determinant \(\pm \partial_\kappa \left[ t \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \neq 0\), hence, by the inverse function theorem, a chart around \(p\) in the maximal atlas. \(\square\)
